docs.d: Install FVM and run your first project.

s.b: FVM lets each project use its own Flutter version. Projects on the same version share one installed SDK. You do not need Dart or Flutter installed first.

s.h: Install script for macOS and Linux
s.b: Run the install script: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/install.sh sh You need curl, an unzip tool (unzip or Python 3), and a checksum tool (sha256sum, shasum, or openssl). Run the setup command printed by the installer. For the default location: "$HOME/.fvm/bin/fvm" setup --write-path-line Setup backs up your shell startup file and adds the PATH entries. Open a new terminal and check: fvm --version If the installer reports a conflicting fvm function or alias, follow its instructions before running setup.

1. Open FVM releases. Download fvm-windows-x64.zip and its matching .sha256 file from the same release. 2. Run Get-FileHash .\fvm-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 in PowerShell and compare the hash with the .sha256 file. 3. Extract fvm.exe to a permanent folder, such as C:\Tools\fvm. 4. Run setup using its full path: & "C:\Tools\fvm\fvm.exe" setup Add the executable's folder and the shims folder printed by setup to your user PATH in Windows Environment Variables. Put the shims folder before other Flutter installations. Open a new terminal and run fvm --version.

On macOS or Linux, set FVM_HOME to choose an installation directory: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/install.sh FVM_HOME="$HOME/tools/fvm" sh Set FVM_HOME to that same directory in your shell startup file for future commands, then run the setup command printed by the installer. To choose a specific FVM release, set FVM_VERSION on the installer process instead. For example, use FVM_VERSION=" " sh at the end of the install command, replacing the placeholder with a version from FVM releases.

From your Flutter project's root directory: fvm install stable fvm use stable --gitignore fvm flutter --version install stable downloads the current stable release. use stable saves that release's version number in .fvmrc. The project stays on that version until you choose another one. For a specific release, use fvm use 3.44.0 --gitignore, replacing the version with the one you need. FVM installs it if necessary. Find available releases with fvm list-remote. Commit .fvmrc and the .gitignore change. Keep .fvm/ out of Git.

Read the version in .fvmrc, then select it. For {"flutter": "3.44.0"}: fvm use 3.44.0 fvm flutter pub get This installs the SDK if needed and creates the editor link on your computer. Running fvm flutter alone does not install a missing SDK.

In VS Code, merge this setting into your project's .vscode/settings.json: { "dart.flutterSdkPath": ".fvm/flutter_sdk" } In Android Studio or IntelliJ, set the Flutter SDK path to the full path of .fvm/flutter_sdk inside your project. Restart the editor if it still shows the previous SDK.
fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter run fvm flutter test fvm dart analyze Use fvm dart for the Dart bundled with your project's Flutter SDK. Plain dart keeps your existing Dart setup.

After the setup step above, plain flutter also follows your project's version. From a configured project, check: flutter --version fvm which fvm doctor FVM's launcher, called a shim, must come before other Flutter installations on PATH. Follow fvm doctor if the wrong version runs. To manage PATH yourself, run fvm setup and follow its printed instructions. On Windows, update your user PATH manually; PowerShell does not support --write-path-line. If you move the FVM executable, run setup from its new location. To undo the automatic PATH edit, run fvm setup --remove-path-line and open a new terminal. This leaves manually added PATH entries and installed SDKs in place.

Manage versions: project pins, channels, aliases, and defaults. Commands: all FVM commands and options. Update FVM and Flutter. Run in CI. Troubleshoot your setup. Documentation for AI assistants is also available.

docs.d: Project pins, channels, aliases, and defaults.

s.b: From your project's root directory: fvm use 3.44.0 --gitignore FVM installs the version if needed, writes .fvmrc, and updates .fvm/flutter_sdk for your editor: {"flutter": "3.44.0"} Commit .fvmrc and the .gitignore change; keep .fvm/ out of Git. Teammates run fvm use with that version after cloning. See editor setup.

Commands use the nearest .fvmrc in your current directory or a parent. Running fvm use in a subdirectory updates that same pin. To give a nested project its own version, run this from its root: fvm use 3.44.0 --here --gitignore

FVM also accepts a bare version on one line, or a JSON flutter value naming a channel or alias. Those names must be available on every computer. Prefer the concrete version number written by fvm use for shared projects.

To select the current stable release: fvm install stable fvm use stable Install the channel first so FVM knows its version. use stable saves the version number, so later channel updates do not move the project. Repeat both commands when you want to upgrade. beta works the same way. Historical dev releases may appear in fvm list-remote --channel dev; main and master builds are not supported.

fvm alias work 3.44.0 fvm use work fvm alias list fvm unalias work Aliases are local to your computer. fvm use work saves the version number in .fvmrc, so teammates do not need your alias. Removing the alias leaves the SDK installed. If you manually put a channel or alias in .fvmrc, FVM uses its saved value on your computer. It does not fetch a new release when you run Flutter. Refresh a channel with fvm install stable or fvm install beta.

Choose a version for directories without a project pin: fvm global 3.44.0 FVM installs the version if needed. Run fvm global without an argument to view the default. To choose stable, run fvm install stable followed by fvm global stable; this also saves a specific version number.

Run fvm which to see which SDK will run and why. FVM uses the first selection that applies: 1. The FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION environment variable. 2. The nearest .fvmrc in your current directory or a parent. 3. Your global default. 4. Another Flutter installation on PATH. An invalid or missing explicit selection produces an error. Follow its correction or installation command; FVM does not substitute another version.

Install the version first. In a POSIX shell: fvm install 3.44.0 FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION=3.44.0 fvm flutter test In PowerShell: fvm install 3.44.0 $env:FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION = "3.44.0" fvm flutter test Remove-Item Env:FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION The PowerShell variable lasts until you remove it. Neither example changes .fvmrc.

fvm list fvm remove 3.44.0 Projects share installed SDKs, so check your other projects before removing a version. FVM reports references it can detect but cannot discover every project on disk. See removal options.
Run fvm --help for usage. For flutter, dart, and exec, all following arguments—including --help—belong to the tool being run.

Download a Flutter SDK without changing your project pin. fvm install stable fvm install 3.44.0 fvm install 3.44.0 --force Accepts a version, channel, or saved alias. Channels check for their current release. Already installed versions are reused; --force (-f) replaces them. Select the downloaded SDK with fvm use.

Choose a version for the current project. fvm use 3.44.0 --gitignore fvm install stable fvm use stable Installs a missing SDK, writes a concrete version to .fvmrc, and updates .fvm/flutter_sdk. Install a channel before selecting it. --gitignore adds .fvm/ to the project’s .gitignore. --here creates a pin in this directory instead of updating the nearest parent pin. --global (-g) sets the global default instead of a project pin.

Set the default outside pinned projects, or show the current default. fvm global 3.44.0 fvm global Installs a missing SDK. For a channel, run fvm install stable before fvm global stable. Saves a concrete version number. Project pins and FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION take priority.
Show installed versions, project selection, global default, aliases, and channels. fvm list fvm ls is the same command.

Find releases available for your operating system and CPU architecture. fvm list-remote fvm list-remote --channel beta --all Requires a network connection. Defaults to the newest 25 stable releases. --channel (-c) accepts stable, beta, or dev; --all includes older releases.

Delete an installed SDK to free disk space. fvm remove 3.44.0 Check other projects before removing a shared version. If FVM reports references to the SDK, update those pins, defaults, or aliases first. --force (-f) removes it anyway and leaves those references in place. Reinstall it with fvm install if needed.

Save a shortcut for a version, or list saved names. fvm alias work 3.44.0 fvm alias list Creating an alias does not install an SDK. Run fvm use work to install and pin its version. Aliases can target channels or other aliases; avoid loops. Names are local to your computer.
Delete a saved name without deleting the SDK. fvm unalias work Concrete project pins keep working. Update any manually written pins or other aliases that refer to the removed name.

Explain the Flutter SDK selected for your current directory. fvm which fvm which --path --path prints only the Flutter executable path for scripts. fvm current is another name for this command. See resolution order.

Run Flutter using the selected SDK. fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter run fvm flutter test fvm flutter --help Arguments and exit status pass through to Flutter. Install the selected SDK first; running Flutter does not download a missing SDK.

Run the Dart bundled with the selected Flutter SDK. fvm dart --version fvm dart analyze fvm dart format . fvm dart run tool/generate.dart Uses Flutter’s Dart even if another Dart SDK is on PATH. Arguments and exit status pass through to Dart.

Run a tool or script with the selected Flutter and Dart first on PATH. fvm exec dart analyze fvm exec sh tool/check.sh Replace the script path with your own. The command and tools it starts use the selected SDK. Your terminal’s PATH is unchanged afterward. All arguments belong to the child command; FVM returns its exit status.

Create the Flutter launcher and configure your shell. fvm setup fvm setup --write-path-line Plain setup prints PATH instructions. --write-path-line backs up and edits the shell startup file; reopen the terminal afterward. On Windows, edit user PATH manually. --remove-path-line removes the line setup added, leaving manual entries and SDKs in place. --fvm-path= selects the FVM executable the launcher uses. If fvm is not on PATH, use its full installed path. See shell setup.

Check SDK selection, project pins, editor links, and shell conflicts. fvm doctor Run this from the affected project and follow the corrections it prints. To check platform build tools and devices, use fvm flutter doctor.

Read or save the color preference for FVM output. fvm config color fvm config color auto Modes are auto, always, and never. Auto respects NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb. Override one invocation with fvm --color=never list. Flutter and Dart control their own output.

Update FVM while keeping installed SDKs and project pins. fvm update --check fvm update --check reports availability without installing. Use fvm update for a specific FVM release. See updating to update Flutter instead.

fvm update --check fvm update --check reports whether an update is available. fvm update installs it. Your Flutter SDKs and project pins stay in place. You can also rerun the installer. To install a specific FVM release, use fvm update with a version from FVM releases.

From your project directory: fvm install stable fvm use stable fvm flutter --version fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter test The first command downloads the current stable release. The second updates .fvmrc and your editor's SDK link. Commit the changed .fvmrc after checking your app. For a specific release, use fvm use instead. Other projects keep their saved versions.

s.h: Update the default for unpinned directories
s.b: fvm install stable fvm global stable
Use --no-version-check for a command where you do not want FVM update notices: fvm --no-version-check flutter test

docs.d: Install and test your project in CI.

s.b: Commit .fvmrc with a concrete Flutter version. On a macOS or Linux runner, this example installs FVM, makes it available to the current shell, and tests a project pinned to 3.44.0: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrgnhnt96/fvm/main/install.sh sh export PATH="${FVM_HOME:-$HOME/.fvm}/bin:$PATH" fvm install 3.44.0 fvm flutter pub get fvm flutter test Replace 3.44.0 with the version in your project's .fvmrc. Run the Flutter commands from the checked-out project directory. For Windows runners, use the Windows installation steps. Use your CI provider's environment or PATH mechanism if installation and testing run in separate steps. A shell's export may not carry over to the next step. You do not need shell setup when invoking Flutter through fvm flutter. Use fvm exec for scripts that call Flutter or Dart themselves.

Cache $FVM_HOME/versions (default: ~/.fvm/versions) between jobs. Include the operating system, CPU architecture, and pinned Flutter version in the cache key. Keep the install command so a job also works with an empty cache.
Install the version before overriding the project pin. In a POSIX shell: fvm install 3.44.0 FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION=3.44.0 fvm flutter test A failing Flutter command returns a failing exit status to CI.

docs.d: Fix command, SDK, and editor problems.

s.h: The fvm command is not found
s.b: With the default macOS or Linux installation, run: "$HOME/.fvm/bin/fvm" setup --write-path-line Open a new terminal and run fvm --version. For a custom installation, use the executable path printed by the installer. On Windows, add the directories printed by setup to your user PATH, then open a new terminal. If the executable is missing, install FVM again.

An old shell function, alias, or PATH entry may take priority. Run the installed executable by its full path with doctor, for example: "$HOME/.fvm/bin/fvm" doctor Remove the conflicting setup identified in the output, rerun setup, and open a new terminal.

fvm which fvm doctor Check whether FVM_FLUTTER_VERSION, a parent .fvmrc, or your global default is selecting the version. Change the project version with fvm use . If fvm flutter --version is correct but flutter --version is not, repeat Shell Setup. The FVM launcher must come first on PATH.

Run the fvm install command printed in the error. For a new project checkout, run fvm use with the version from .fvmrc to install it and create the editor link. If FVM does not recognize stable or beta, install that channel first: fvm install stable fvm use stable

Check your network connection and proxy settings, then retry. FVM downloads its own updates from GitHub and Flutter SDKs from Google's Flutter storage. For a damaged SDK, reinstall its version: fvm install 3.44.0 --force If the release is unavailable for your computer, use fvm list-remote to find a supported version. If a checksum mismatch persists, do not use that download.

Run fvm use again and set the editor's Flutter SDK path to .fvm/flutter_sdk beside .fvmrc. Restart the editor. See Editor setup for the VS Code setting. If Windows reports that it cannot create the SDK link, follow the error's instructions about permissions or Developer Mode, then rerun fvm use.

s.h: Using standalone Dart or another manager
s.b: Use fvm dart --version to check the Dart bundled with your project's Flutter SDK. Plain dart may use a separate installation, including DVM. .dvmrc selects standalone Dart; .fvmrc selects Flutter. Use fvm exec for scripts that need both Flutter and its Dart on PATH. These docs describe mrgnhnt96/fvm, which is separate from the pub.dev package named fvm. If you keep both managers, choose which executable PATH should find and give this one a separate FVM_HOME. Existing SDK caches are not imported; install the versions you need with fvm install.
fvm --verbose flutter --version Use this alongside fvm doctor when you need more detail about a failure.
